name: cboe_short_vol
claim: A short-premium book is a distinct, high-probability return engine for 25-50% of capital
tasty_value: Keep 25-50% of buying power in options, max 75%; skew higher in high volatility and small accounts
tasty_note: Allocation guidance, not a return claim; tastylive does not frame it against the S&P 500.
our_value: Since 2009-03-09 6/6 short-vol indices trailed the S&P 500 TR (16.88%); 2007-2026 betas to the S&P PUT 0.60, BXM 0.62, BXMD 0.80, WPUT 0.53, CNDR 0.10, BFLY 0.06.
data: Cboe index history CSVs (cdn.cboe.com/api/global/us_indices/daily_prices/<NAME>_History.csv): PUT, BXM, BXMD, WPUT, CNDR, BFLY (PPUT for comparison); Yahoo ^SP500TR, ^IRX
method: CAGR from daily closes; vol, Sharpe (vs ^IRX) and beta from month-end returns; max drawdown and episode peak-to-trough on daily closes. Phase 03's computed_stats are re-derived and compared within stated tolerances (phase03_check).
caveats: Gross index returns: no commissions, no bid-ask (Cboe indices trade at stated prices), no taxes. Real implementations lag the index.
Cboe publishes these indices and sponsored most of the early studies of them.
The S&P 500 TR comes from Yahoo ^SP500TR; Sharpe uses month-end returns and ^IRX, so it can differ by about +/-0.05 from other conventions.
PUT's Cboe file is sparse before 2007-01-03, so PUT starts there; BXM's file starts 2002-03-22 and WPUT's 2006-01-31.
Cboe has no undefined-risk strangle index; CNDR has 5-delta wings, so it is not the tastylive naked strangle (see repro:strangle_mgmt for a model-priced one).

claims.text: Selling premium beats buying it over time
claims.tasty_value: tastylive's core premise: implied volatility often overstates realized, so sellers are paid for the gap (no figure given on the page)
claims.tasty_note: Qualitative on the pages reviewed; the archive's premium-selling studies were not extracted in full.
claims.our_value: 2007-2026: selling ATM SPX puts (PUT, 7.24% CAGR) earned +5.68 pts/yr over its T-bill collateral (1.56%); buying 5% OTM puts on the S&P (PPUT, 8.14%) cost -2.82 pts/yr vs the S&P 500 TR (10.95%).

claims.text: Defined-risk wings give up much of the edge
claims.tasty_value: A 16-delta condor with 5-delta wings keeps about 60% of the strangle's median P&L with about 38% less tail risk and 2.5x less buying power (SPY, 2005-2021)
claims.tasty_note: Agrees in direction: tastylive also finds the wings cost about 40% of profit.
claims.our_value: CNDR (20-delta short strangle + 5-delta wings) 0.98% CAGR 2007-2026 vs PUT 7.24% and T-bills 1.56%.
